title: CyberLeek eight-domain research screening catalogue
challenge: 2026 Space Apps - Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars
scientificStatus: Expert-curated qualitative research experiment suitability profiles. Not universally measured NASA physical readings, not a validated lander safety model, not a global exhaustive search.
featureTags: Controlled project tags describing possible Earth field-test utility, not field-measured abundances.
scoring: Domain: 100 × (0.7×goal coverage + 0.3×trait precision) × planet/domain transfer factor. Weighted eight-domain score blended with optional latitude-regime operational prior. Click distance is a separate confidence warning, not an index multiplier. No NASA calibration.

domains.label: Geology & materials
domains.question: Which rocks, minerals and deposits can we practice sampling?
domains.data: NASA/USGS planetary geologic maps; LROC, THEMIS; geological site descriptions.

domains.label: Terrain & topography
domains.question: What landforms and traversal problems are comparable?
domains.data: NASA MOLA Mars DEM; LRO/LOLA Moon DEM; Copernicus and Earth terrain models.

domains.label: Temperature & illumination
domains.question: Can we practice in relevant heat, cold or lighting conditions?
domains.data: NASA POWER Earth climate; LRO Diviner temperatures; Moon illumination mapping; Mars THEMIS.

domains.label: Water, ice & resources
domains.question: Can resource prospecting, drilling or sampling be exercised?
domains.data: NASA/agency cryosphere products; LRO polar maps; Mars MOLA/SHARAD and SWIM reports.

domains.label: Dust, wind & surface processes
domains.question: What surface processing can we imitate without confusing air and vacuum?
domains.data: NASA POWER wind and Earth aerosols; Martian THEMIS imagery; lunar surface/regolith observations.

domains.label: Biology & biosignatures
domains.question: How can sampling, preservation and contamination control be tested?
domains.data: NASA astrobiology analog field descriptions; laboratory and field biosignature research.

domains.label: Caves & underground
domains.question: Could subsurface scouting, imaging or drilling be tested?
domains.data: NASA/JPL candidate pit imagery; Earth field geology, documented lava tubes and ice-cemented ground.

domains.label: Exploration & operations
domains.question: Does this field site support meaningful hardware and mission trials?
domains.data: NASA analog mission and fieldwork reports; terrain and logistical context (not an accessibility clearance).

earth.name: Yungay / Atacama Desert
earth.reason: Extreme dry-soil and biosignature testing analog. Famous site, included as a benchmark.

geology.summary: Arid desert soils and mineral alteration context; not a generic basaltic shield volcano.

terrain.summary: Dry, rocky or sediment-covered plains support sampling and route-planning trials.

thermal.summary: Very arid conditions, strong daytime solar exposure and diurnal thermal cycles.

resources.summary: Scarce accessible surface water supports dry-resource prospecting experiments.

dust.summary: Windblown desert particles support aeolian transport and instrument-dust screening.

biology.summary: Extremely low-biomass soil investigations are useful for biosignature detection and contamination controls.

subsurface.summary: Subsurface soil sampling and layer-preservation tests; no lava tube claimed at the map point.

operations.summary: Accessible in some areas for specialist campaigns; permits and safety must be separately assessed.

earth.name: Haughton Impact Crater
earth.reason: NASA-proven Arctic impact structure and remote expedition operations benchmark.

geology.summary: Meteorite-impact crater and shocked rock geology; not a volcanic shield.

terrain.summary: Impact crater, rocky rough terrain and exposed slopes for rover hazard comparison.

thermal.summary: Freezing Arctic temperatures and strong polar seasonal light cycles.

resources.summary: Polar ground and seasonally frozen terrain offer ice-handling scenario research.

dust.summary: Loose polar sediment and granular abrasion can be studied; no direct lunar vacuum match.

biology.summary: Cold-desert contamination-control research, despite Earth microbiology.

subsurface.summary: Crater sediments and frozen-ground coring are relevant; crater is not a verified cave.

operations.summary: Documented NASA rover/exploration-operations analog in isolated extreme terrain.

earth.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
earth.reason: Polar, hyper-arid, microbe-bearing landscape especially useful for cold subsurface exploration.

geology.summary: Exposed polar desert sediments, rock and weathering products.

terrain.summary: Polar valleys, rocky ground and ice-cemented surfaces.

thermal.summary: Extreme cold, dryness and polar illumination regime.

resources.summary: Ice-cemented ground and nearby ice provide drill-sampling analog contexts.

dust.summary: Dry sediment, erosion and particle transport under Earth winds.

biology.summary: NASA describes cryptoendolithic microbes and preserved biosignatures in this harsh setting.

subsurface.summary: Ice-cemented subsurface soil and rock are relevant drilling subjects.

operations.summary: Remote polar field operations, traverse planning and restricted environmental access.

earth.name: Fagradalsfjall Lava Field
earth.reason: Recent lava flow and volcanic vent processes investigated by NASA field teams.

geology.summary: Recent basaltic volcanic lava and vents for field spectroscopy and morphology.

terrain.summary: Lava flows, cones and broken rock; active-hazard zones require monitoring.

thermal.summary: Cold North Atlantic conditions with volcanic thermal anomalies; not a permanent thermal proxy.

resources.summary: Fresh volcanic rock enables sample and material-processing trials.

dust.summary: Fresh fragmental rock can simulate gritty surface handling.

biology.summary: NASA field studies investigate sampling protocols and life-detection methods on Icelandic volcanics.

subsurface.summary: Volcanic flow structure offers subsurface-geology questions; no mapped tube is asserted here.

operations.summary: NASA has used Iceland volcanic fieldwork for science-instrument and traverse exercises.

earth.name: Lava Beds National Monument
earth.reason: Documented basaltic flows and lava tubes support lunar subsurface reconnaissance.

geology.summary: NPS describes basalt-to-rhyolite volcanic flows with cinder cones and other features.

terrain.summary: Rough lava flows, vents and varied volcanic relief.

thermal.summary: Seasonally variable terrestrial conditions; light/dark caves support instrument practice.

resources.summary: Volcanic rock and subsurface material research opportunities; not a verified ice resource analog.

dust.summary: Broken lava fragments and unconsolidated volcanic surfaces.

biology.summary: Earth cave biology requires strict biosafety; useful for contamination-avoidance trials.

subsurface.summary: Documented lava tubes make this a strong field analog for cave entry and mapping.

operations.summary: Cave navigation, surface rover traverses and equipment trials could be designed where permitted.

earth.name: Badwater / Death Valley
earth.reason: Hot dry basin and exposed salts; vehicles are not allowed off established roads at Badwater.

geology.summary: Salt and sedimentary basin deposits, not a basaltic mare or impact crater.

terrain.summary: Relatively level basin floors and rugged neighboring badlands.

thermal.summary: High heat, intense sunlight and dry conditions.

resources.summary: Evaporite salts offer resource-detection analog questions, but not frozen water.

dust.summary: Wind-driven dust, sand and erosion provide dust-interface tests.

biology.summary: Dryland biosignature and contamination exercises; not a sterile planet stand-in.

subsurface.summary: Desert sediment coring scenarios; no cave is assumed at Badwater.

operations.summary: Badwater salt-flat surfaces are protected: no off-road vehicle testing; permitted observation and sampling proposals would require park approval.

earth.name: Kīlauea Volcanic Field
earth.reason: Basalt landscapes and volcanic tubes provide geology and subsurface analogs.

geology.summary: Basaltic eruptions, lava sheets and volcanic vents.

terrain.summary: Broken and smooth lava surfaces with rough volcanic relief.

thermal.summary: Warm and humid Earth setting; very different from lunar vacuum or Martian cold.

resources.summary: Basalt and volcanic material support construction-feedstock concepts.

dust.summary: Volcanic ash and rock grains support materials characterization.

biology.summary: Life-colonization gradients across young lava support contamination and biosignature tests.

subsurface.summary: NASA astrobiology lists lava tubes for studying possible ancient-Mars subsurface habitats.

operations.summary: Geological traverse and instruments testing potential where safe and authorized.

earth.name: Craters of the Moon
earth.reason: Rocky basaltic flow fields and lava tubes for lunar volcanic-route simulations.

geology.summary: Basaltic fissure eruptions, cinder cones and lava fields.

terrain.summary: Rough lava, fissures, cones and relatively open lava plains.

thermal.summary: Dry continental conditions with pronounced daily and seasonal temperature variation.

resources.summary: Exposed basalt and volcanic rubble for engineering-material handling.

dust.summary: Fine volcanic particles and broken lava rubble for regolith-handling exercises.

biology.summary: Sample cleanliness and pioneering vegetation studies, not sterile planetary conditions.

subsurface.summary: Documented lava tubes and fissures for cave-navigation research.

operations.summary: Rugged but comparatively accessible volcanic field for traverse demonstrations, subject to park rules.

targets.name: Hecates Tholus
targets.mission: Test lava-and-ice geological interpretation and rough volcanic rover operations.
targets.limitations: Low pressure, Mars gravity, radiation, and global dust cannot be reproduced outdoors on Earth.

geology.observation: Volcanic edifice in NASA-mapped Elysium volcanic province; site mineral fractions not sampled here.

terrain.observation: Volcano flanks and relief in MOLA terrain; patch-scale rover hazards need finer maps.

thermal.observation: Martian cold and strong diurnal contrasts; no verified local weather series included.

resources.observation: Ancient glacier-related landforms have been discussed; present ice abundance at this pin is unverified.

dust.observation: Martian surface particles and atmospheric dust processes require windblown-grit tests.

biology.observation: No confirmed Martian life; contamination-aware biosignature sampling is a test objective.

subsurface.observation: Volcanic/ice contact motivates drilling and soil-core tests; no confirmed local tube is claimed.

operations.observation: Volcanic traverse and remote sensing are appropriate research concepts, not approved landing plans.

targets.name: Elysium Mons
targets.mission: Choose an Earth volcanic field for basalt mineral analysis, lava-flow mapping and rover testing.
targets.limitations: Earth basalt is weathered and biologically active; Mars has different gravity, atmosphere and radiation.

geology.observation: Large Martian shield volcano mapped in the NASA MOLA Elysium region.

terrain.observation: Broad shield volcano and flank lava-flow morphology; DEM cells are regional.

thermal.observation: Cold, thin-atmosphere Mars conditions; aim for dry field operations.

resources.observation: Volcanic rock/regolith resources are a sampling objective; site ice quantity not measured here.

dust.observation: Surface soil and aeolian grit can affect rover instruments.

biology.observation: No confirmed Martian life; use contamination-aware sampling and instruments testing.

subsurface.observation: Volcanic units motivate shallow coring; no cave has been confirmed at this chosen point.

operations.observation: Rover traction, mineral mapping and rough-track sampling are useful field-test objectives.

targets.name: Albor Tholus
targets.mission: Investigate cratered volcanic relief and steep-slope mobility on Earth.
targets.limitations: Earth crater/volcano operations cannot reproduce Martian low-pressure atmosphere and gravity.

geology.observation: NASA THEMIS shows a volcano with a pronounced caldera in the Elysium province.

terrain.observation: Steep caldera relief and volcanic flank terrain; precise safe routes need site DEM.

thermal.observation: Cold, dusty Martian environment; no measured site-specific thermal series used.

resources.observation: Basaltic volcanic materials are a collection target; no measured local ice inventory.

dust.observation: Grit and rockfall accumulation can be an operational process analog.

biology.observation: No confirmed indigenous life; clean sampling remains mission-relevant.

subsurface.observation: Crater/flank drilling and layer examination are analog objectives, not evidence of a known cave.

operations.observation: Steep terrain requires cautious routing and hazard scouting.

targets.name: Apollo 11 / Tranquility Base
targets.mission: Find basaltic Earth terrain suited to regolith handling, flat-ground rover trials and sample geology.
targets.limitations: No Earth field site reproduces lunar vacuum, one-sixth gravity, radiation or real lunar dust properties.

geology.observation: NASA describes the Mare Tranquillitatis basin as relatively smooth basaltic lava plains.

terrain.observation: Relatively smooth mare with impact overprints; rover-scale roughness not computed here.

thermal.observation: Vacuum exposure causes extreme day/night heating and cooling; outdoors only partially analog.

resources.observation: Regolith and local basalt materials are relevant; no local exposed ice is established.

dust.observation: Lunar abrasive regolith has no wind transport; test loose-grain handling, not aeolian physics.

biology.observation: No confirmed indigenous lunar life; contamination control is the Earth-test objective.

subsurface.observation: Lunar mare volcanic structures motivate optional lava-tube methods; no tube is claimed at Apollo 11.

operations.observation: Sample collection, rover handling and navigation across rocky plains.

targets.name: Shackleton crater / South Pole
targets.mission: Find a cold crater or polar Earth site for ice prospecting, difficult lighting and remote traverse tests.
targets.limitations: Permanent shadows, lunar gravity and cryogenic-vacuum chemistry require separate laboratory testing.

geology.observation: NASA maps an impact crater in ancient polar highlands; precise mineralogy varies.

terrain.observation: Steep crater rim and permanently shadowed interior require hazard-aware planning.

thermal.observation: Rim sunlight and permanently shadowed cold floors; Earth seasonal polar darkness is only partial analog.

resources.observation: Polar cold traps may host water ice; this prototype makes no local ice-grade estimate.

dust.observation: Airless lunar regolith and dust adhesion are important; terrestrial gritty soil is a handling analog only.

biology.observation: No confirmed lunar life; clean ice coring and contamination control are useful test scenarios.

subsurface.observation: Cold subsurface and shadowed material motivate ice coring, not a confirmed cave.

operations.observation: Remote polar route planning, prospecting, robotic hazard mapping and sampling.

targets.name: Aristarchus Plateau
targets.mission: Discover lava-field and subsurface analogs for pyroclastic deposits, sinuous rilles and traverse science.
targets.limitations: The actual lunar pyroclastic chemistry, vacuum, reduced gravity and dust charging are different from Earth.

geology.observation: NASA maps volcanic pyroclastic mantling and basaltic flows in the Aristarchus region.

terrain.observation: Sinuous rilles, crater margins and volcanic relief create complex routing challenges.

thermal.observation: Airless day/night heat extremes demand instrument thermal testing beyond any Earth field match.

resources.observation: Pyroclastic material and possible volcanic volatiles motivate resource characterization, not proven ore.

dust.observation: Loose pyroclastic material and abrasive grains motivate handling tests, not lunar wind analogs.

biology.observation: No confirmed indigenous life; field tests can validate sample cleanliness.

subsurface.observation: Sinuous rilles suggest volcanic channels/collapse; their cavities are not verified at this map point.

operations.observation: Rover imaging, vent stratigraphy, sample handling and rough route planning.
